text: - A snapshot the replay rebuilds from the log writes one `state-recovered` line into the role file of the process that read it (`cli-<name>.ndjson`, `mcp.ndjson`, `hook-<name>.ndjson` or `run-<name>.ndjson`), from each replay reader: `live_endpoint` (the CLI frame verbs and `mcp`'s frame tools), hook `connect`, statusline `serve` and `run`'s collision check, beside `viola revive` and `viola list`. `viola revive`'s preflight reads the snapshot once for both its collision check and its recorded-directory reading, so one replay writes one line.

subject: res-filesystem
text:
- `instances/<ViolaName>/events.ndjson`, `events.ndjson.lock`, `snapshot.json`, `snapshot.json.lock`, `heartbeat`, `settings.json` (the per-session settings override that wraps the statusline; Unix only, see Claude Code integration names), `diagnostics/` (the owner-only content-bearing detail files `detail-<role>.ndjson`, such as the panic payload and backtrace in `detail-run.ndjson`; dir 0700, files 0600 on Unix; one `write` per line; file format owned by obs and fixed by `schemas/diag-detail.v1.json`. Codes-only process lines go to the home-level role files). v1 never rotates or truncates `events.ndjson`, because `wait`'s `after` and `send`'s `cursor` are byte offsets into it. Bounding its size is an open item, and any scheme must keep existing offsets valid. These entry points check these files before they use them: `viola list`; `viola revive`; `viola run`'s start (through `check_home_tree` with its name); `viola hook`'s statusline, event and dialog paths (sharing `trusted`); `viola mcp`'s frame tools; and the CLI frame verbs `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link` and `unlink` (sharing `client::refuse_untrusted`). `viola list` (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list): `viola_state::board::scan` runs `check_path` on the home and on `instances/`, each that exists (absent passes, an unstattable one is refused), reads each entry's type without following a link (a link, a non-directory or a name that is no `ViolaName` gives no instance and is only counted), joins a path only from a parsed name, then runs `check_instance` per instance in name order, all before any file under the home is opened and before its log starts; the first failure refuses the whole board with exit 21 (`--json`: `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` on stdout, stderr empty; human: the instance-state or the home-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair on stderr, stdout empty), no log opened, no line written and the home's mode left as found — the founder's own answer, 2026-10-13, relayed verbatim by the Viola overseer (the operator's answer at that chunk's planning, superseded 2026-10-13).
 `viola revive` (the start arm and `--list`) runs `viola_state::strict::check_instance` over the home (the read rule), `instances/` (the write rule), the instance directory (the read rule), its `diagnostics/` (the read rule), its `snapshot.json` (the write rule) and its `events.ndjson` (the write rule on Unix, the read rule on Windows), each that exists and a folder before what it holds, before its wrapper log opens, and a refusal is exit 1 with the state-files `unable:` / `hint:` pair (under `--json` the `{"v":1,"error":"strict-modes-failed","detail":null}` document on stdout, stderr empty): no log opened, no line written (no `process-start`, no `process-exit`), no child started and the home's mode left as found. `viola hook statusline` runs the same check on its canonicalised instance directory before anything under the home is read or opened; a refused instance returns exit 0 at once with no `config.json` read, no role file opened, no `hook-invoked` or `hook-decision` line, no stdin read, no command run, nothing printed and `budget.json` untouched. Neither arm writes the word `strict-modes-failed` on any line. `viola link` / `viola unlink` run `check_instance` on the home and `instances/<driven>` before `client::start`, so before any role file or log opens and before any snapshot value is read; a refusal is exit 21 (`--json` the `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` document on stdout, stderr empty; human the instance-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair on stderr), no line written and the mode left as found. Each of these checks comes first because opening a log sets an existing home to 0700 (as measured on the statusline arm at chunk 2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through, `evidence/red-green.md` §3), and a check made after it passes a home at 0770. Both orders were fixed at chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor: before it `revive`'s start arm opened its log first, and a home at 0770 came back 0700 and passed the check (as measured at that chunk's `research.md`, runs C and D, and `evidence/red-green.md` (a)), and the statusline arm opened its log after a refused check, so its refusal lasted one invocation (`evidence/red-green.md` (b)). That a refused check leaves no trace on the statusline arm is the founder's own answer, 2026-10-13, relayed verbatim by the Viola overseer (the operator's answer at that chunk's planning, superseded 2026-10-13). `check_instance` has these three product call sites (`src/cmd/hook.rs` `trusted`, shared by the statusline, event and dialog paths; `src/cmd/revive.rs`; and `src/cmd/client.rs` `refuse_untrusted`, shared by `link` / `unlink` and the six frame verbs; the rule: `check_instance(` under `src/`). Outside that rule `viola-mcp`'s `tools.rs` `frame` calls it, and `run`'s start reaches its set through `viola_state::strict::check_home_tree`.
 The check is proven on Unix (five widened modes). On Windows `cfg(windows)` cases prove it: an instance tree granted Users write is refused `Writable` beside a `create_private_dir` tree that passes, a `diagnostics/` granted Users read is refused, and a plain home made before viola is refused for its inherited write grant to a SID `trusted_sid` does not trust, read by its right whichever SID holds it, while a home `instance_tree()` makes reads none (as measured at ci#40439188053, `windows-2025`).

subject: res-filesystem
text: - `viola_state::strict` holds two rules. The read rule is the write rule plus, on Unix, a refusal of any group or other bit (`mode & 0o077`) and, on Windows, a refusal of any allow ACE, an inherit-only one included, that grants a right in `READ_RIGHTS` (`0x9000_0001`: `FILE_READ_DATA` | `GENERIC_READ` | `GENERIC_ALL`) to a SID `trusted_sid` rejects (`unix_read_verdict`, `windows_read_verdict`, `check_read`). `Refused` holds `Readable` for a read-rule refusal and `Symlink` for a symbolic link `check_diagnostics` meets, each with a fixed message.

subject: res-filesystem
text: - `viola_state::strict::check_home_tree(home, name, key)` checks the home (the read rule); with a name, `check_instance`'s set; then `ledger/`, `bin/` and `plugin/`; with a key, `bin/<key>/`, the pinned `viola` (`viola.exe` on Windows), `plugin/<key>/`, its `hooks/` and its `.claude-plugin/` (the write rule). It checks only entries that exist and refuses as `TreeRefused::HomeLevel` or `TreeRefused::InstanceLevel`. `run`'s start and `viola revive`'s start call it through `checked_exe` (the instance's name and the `pin_key` of the exe bytes read once), and `verify` calls it with no name and no key.

subject: res-filesystem
text: - The other checked entry points run the instance check first, each refusing with nothing under the home opened, no line written and the mode or ACL left as found: the CLI frame verbs `send` (after its text read), `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause` and `release` through `client::refuse_untrusted`, which `link` / `unlink` share, before any snapshot value is read (their exits: Binaries, above); `viola hook`'s event and dialog paths through `trusted`, before `read_diagnostics_level` and obs init, with its two `--capture` arms ahead of it (exit 0, with no `config.json` read, role file, stdin read, frame or SessionEnd append); `viola mcp`'s frame tools before `live_endpoint` (`instance-unreachable` with `detail: null`, no frame); and `viola run`'s and `viola revive`'s starts through `check_home_tree` before `open_wrapper_log` (the home pair, or the instance pair for an instance-level refusal, and no child).

subject: res-filesystem
text: - A path under a regular file stats `NotFound` on Windows, so the strict-modes check skips it as absent and the `cli` catch-site line stands there; on Unix the same home is a strict-modes refusal (`verify` exits 1 with the home pair, the frame verbs exit 21 with the instance pair). A test that plants a regular file above a checked path therefore needs a per-OS oracle (as measured at ci#40398601594, `windows-2025`).

subject: res-filesystem
text: - `viola list`'s two home checks disagree: `board::scan`'s own `check_path` holds the home to the write rule while `check_instance` holds it to the read rule, so a 0750 home passes a board with no instance and is refused (`ScanRefused::Instance`) once it holds one. Their reconciliation is owed to a CARRY on the working-route entry "Unix endpoint and home hardening".

subject: res-filesystem
text: - `ledger/stamps.json` + `ledger/stamps.json.lock`: `viola verify` stamps (CLI version → each ledger row's `pass`/`fail`, plus the values measured for that version: `largest_hook_payload` per spine event and `typed_probe`, the interactive runs' ready and turn settle times, prompt latency, largest turn gap and `/compact` answer latency, which validate the compiled gate and window constants (the compact latency against `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW`), and `dialog_probe.parallel_both_before_first_post`, read from Run C's captures; `run` reads none of them), in the Ledger stamps envelope (Standard Contracts). `ledger/` is 0700 and both files 0600 on Unix. The ONE writer is `viola_state::stamps::update_stamps`, called only by `viola verify`: it runs `strict::check_stamps(home)` before it creates `ledger/` and again under the lock before the capped read, a refusal (`StampsError::StrictModes`) reading and writing nothing and `verify` printing the home pair with exit 1; it holds the `.lock` for the read-modify-write, reads the current bytes under the `MAX_FRAME` cap and replaces through `replace_private`. Readers use `read_stamps` (no lock; over the cap is an error), except `run`'s version gate, which reads through `read_stamps_strict` (the `viola_state::strict` check first: owner-only modes on Unix, owner + DACL on Windows); a refusal records `cli_verified:false` and one `parse-rejected{parser:"ledger-stamps", detail:"strict-modes-failed"}`. The rows themselves (probes and expected post-conditions) are compiled into `viola-agent-claude`. Read by `run`'s version gate.

subject: res-filesystem
text: - Test-only, outside the viola home: `<temp dir>/viola-root-watch/<test name, :: → .>.<label>.report` — the root test support `tests/support/watch.rs` `Watch` (bound `WITHIN` = 7 s, shared by the root waits on a child: `Instant::now() + WITHIN` reads 28 sites in 20 files under `tests/`, as measured at chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor's wrap on the Linux dev host's final tree (two more than at chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive: one each in `tests/cli_budget.rs`, a new file, and `tests/cli_revive.rs`), the shared `tests/support/events.rs` and `tests/support/cli.rs` holding one each; that pattern is the count's rule and not a census of every wait on the bound. One of the waits is `tests/support/home.rs` `wait_endpoint_gone`, which `Wrapper::stop` / `stop_keep` run after the wrapper's exit until the snapshot's recorded `endpoint` is unconnectable; after a kill, `Wrapper::kill` waits on `holder_gone` instead (on Unix a connect to the path is refused or the path is absent, on Windows the pipe is not found), because a killed wrapper removes nothing and its socket file stays on Unix, where the stop path's rule is the file being absent (as measured at chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive, the kill-and-revive case green on the three CI runners)). It is created empty at the wait's start and gets a line only when the polled state changes (codes, counts and booleans only), so a test the runner kills keeps its evidence. It is kept when the test panics or is killed and removed when it passes. `viola` never reads or writes it.

subject: res-filesystem
text: - Test-only: `tests/support/events.rs` holds the error-body check, `error_body_hit` and `assert_error_body_clean`, classes `absolute-path` · `caused-by` · `serde-path` · `planted`, reporting place and class, never bytes. No after-every-test helper is built: the three surface witnesses, the enumeration and the census of writers replace it, reading this check.

text: - An inheritable `icacls` grant (`(OI)(CI)`) on a seeded test home's `bin/`, or on the home, reaches through `seed_conpty`'s hard links into the shared `target/conpty-seed/<key>/` companion and widens every seeded home until it is removed; a test that widens a home tree above `bin/<key>/conpty/` therefore starts that home unseeded, and `seed_conpty` makes the home and the seed dir through `viola_state::fs::create_private_dir` (as measured on `windows-2025` at ci#40398601594 and ci#40400887151).

text: - The protected owner-only DACL of a home viola makes outside the profile reads `D:PAI(A;OICI;FA;;;LA)(A;OICI;FA;;;SY)` on `windows-2025`, read back through `icacls /save`: canonical SDDL spells the runner's user, the local Administrator (RID 500), `LA`, so an oracle matching its SID string fails (as measured at ci#40400887151).

subject: res-repository
text: - On `windows-2025` runners of one image (20261021.278.1) the temp dir's inherited ACL differs by host: Users write on one (ci#40403389629, westus3), Authenticated Users (`S-1-5-11`, mask `0x001301BF`) write with Users read only on another (ci#40425866096, northcentralus). An oracle that names one SID for a runner-inherited grant is runner-dependent, so the plain-home case reads the grant by its right (inherited, a `WRITE_RIGHTS` bit, a SID `trusted_sid` does not trust; `strict::win::tests::inherited_untrusted_writes`), with a control that cannot pass vacuously (as measured at ci#40439188053).
